pr_title: KEP-4330: add forward compatibility for compatibility mode

#### What type of PR is this?
This PR implements the changes proposed in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5038

Two new apiserver cli flags are added:
- `--emulation-forward-compatible` is an option to implicitly enable all APIs which are introduced after the emulation version and have higher priority than APIs of the same group resource enabled at the emulation version.
- `--runtime-config-emulation-forward-compatible` is an option to explicit enable specific APIs introduced after the emulation version through the `runtime-config`.

For example, suppose
`groupA/v1beta1` introduced at 1.31, `groupA/v1beta2` introduced at 1.32 `groupA/v1` introduced at 1.33
`groupB/v1beta1` introduced at 1.32, `groupB/v1` introduced at 1.33
`EmulationVersion=1.31, BinaryVersion=1.33`

flags | enabled versions 
--- | ---
`--runtime-config=groupA/v1beta1=true` | `groupA/v1beta1`
`--runtime-config=groupA/v1beta1 --emulation-forward-compatible` | `groupA/v1beta1`, `groupA/v1beta2`, `groupA/v1`
`--runtime-config=groupA/v1beta1,groupA/v1 ---runtime-config-emulation-forward-compatible` | `groupA/v1beta1`, `groupA/v1`
`--runtime-config=groupB/v1beta1=true` | `error`
`--runtime-config=groupB/v1beta1=true --emulation-forward-compatible` | `error`
`--runtime-config=groupB/v1beta1=true --runtime-config-emulation-forward-compatible` | `groupB/v1beta1`
`--runtime-config=groupB/v1beta1=true --runtime-config-emulation-forward-compatible --emulation-forward-compatible` | `groupB/v1beta1`, `groupB/v1`

issue_context.title: [Compatibility Version] Guidance on API version promotion
comments: /cc @jpbetz @aaron-prindle

I don't see any way around having to support the beta version of API when emulating a controller that only had beta API support at the version being emulated.

But maybe we can find some pattern or offer some utilities to make it easier to support both API versions?

Is this issue still open? I would like to contribute
we can create a generic wrapper that can handle both beta and GA versions of a resource, simplifying the code needed in controllers and other components.
Let me know

> How could we enforce this for users deprecating a Beta API?

Is the new --emulate-version test your adding sufficient?  I was expecting that if the kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager are both run with --emulate-version=1.31 (for binary version 1.32) then the v1beta1 branch of those conditionals would have to work for the test to pass (since the kube-apiserver won't serve v1).

Yes exactly, that is the goal of the test.  I wasn't sure how "shift-left" such an error might need to be but currently the plan for the `--emulate-version` test is that it is is a nightly that is initially not release blocking but eventually is release blocking once after X time of success (no flakes, etc.).  So we should get some signal related to this (eg: a Beta API was removed but --emulated-version support relies on it still being functional), I wasn't sure if it might also be possible to bake something into prerelease-lifecycle-gen or what other options might be for enforcement earlier on in the process

> I don't see any way around having to support the beta version of API when emulating a controller that only had beta API support at the version being emulated.
> 
> But maybe we can find some pattern or offer some utilities to make it easier to support both API versions?

Here's an example of one of my previous type promotion PRs. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122882 It touches the signature of many functions/loops/variable declarations. Will every single spot need to switch on a conditional for emulation version? I don't know the answer for this but depending on the feature it could be a lot of excessive work? If we say allow operations on the v1 resource but convert to v1beta1 when serving, the behavior is transparent to the user. However, there's no doubt that the code has changed and new bugs could have been introduced with the conversion. 

> Would this be part of prerelease-lifecycle-gen or potentially a new linter? Is there single "source of truth" for each release that states each API and it's release lifecycle? (For feature gates, this is somewhat non-trivial for past releases with examining a releases kube_features.go - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127200#discussion_r1768862429)

APIs are a bit different than features in that each one has its own group version and prerelease lifecycle tags. (instead of sharing a single variable toggled between alpha, beta, ga in the case of features). I *think* we can use those as the source of truth? We already use the emulation version in conjunction with those tags to determine which APIs to enable/disable.

> Is the new --emulate-version test your adding sufficient? I was expecting that if the kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager are both run with --emulate-version=1.31 (for binary version 1.32) then the v1beta1 branch of those conditionals would have to work for the test to pass (since the kube-apiserver won't serve v1).

Since we haven't had a beta to GA type promotion in 1.32 yet I'd imagine the tests currently pass but may fail closer to code freeze. Maybe an interesting experiment we can do is to take off the guard rails and try to emulate 1.30? I'd imagine we'll see examples of those problems in prior releases.

> I wasn't sure if it might also be possible to bake something into prerelease-lifecycle-gen or what other options might be for enforcement earlier on in the process

What about yet another linter? :)

I'd be super curious how a linter for this might work.  It feels like it's logic in the code that is hard to identify with a lint rule, but maybe I'm wrong? Or maybe there is a convention we could establish that also happens to be easy to lint?

Siyuan had some interesting logic in the feature gate linter that diffs the unversioned feature list and errors out if something new is added (making it basically impossible for human error to add to the unversioned list unless they edit the yaml by hand). We could add something similar to have a yaml of the APIs and version based on the prerelease lifecycle and detect removals of APIs. The logic would then be that APIs may only be removed (deleted in code) if they've been marked as removed for 3 cycles already.
Relevant to https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/48171
/cc @siyuanfoundation

> I don't see any way around having to support the beta version of API when emulating a controller that only had beta API support at the version being emulated.

I'm with Joe here, all the ways to support emulation seems to require adding code and wrap business logic that means it will be more difficult to debug or troubleshoot problems and much higher risk of having subtle bugs on those features that are already lacking exposure to the users since the "beta off by default", we may start conservative and not allow emulation on those
@aojea Do you mean not allowing emulating beta apis that are disabled by default? Is it practical for upgrade? Beta apis could potentially have high adoption rates
@VishalGawade1 can you share any examples of such wrappers? Thanks!

> Beta apis could potentially have high adoption rates

the problem here is not the beta api itself, is the combo of beta and feature gate that depends on that beta ... since those use to be complex features, we have DynamicResourceAllocation and ServiceCIDR today that I'm aware of, and those require enable the feature gates, I don't think those will get high adoption rates ... and those that are adopting them already have to enable the feature gates to do that

> > Beta apis could potentially have high adoption rates
> 
> the problem here is not the beta api itself, is the combo of beta and feature gate that depends on that beta ... since those use to be complex features, we have DynamicResourceAllocation and ServiceCIDR today that I'm aware of, and those require enable the feature gates, I don't think those will get high adoption rates ... and those that are adopting them already have to enable the feature gates to do that

But we do allow beta features to be emulated. So if the cluster starts to use the beta apis by enabling the beta feature gate, we need support them in emulated version.

> But we do allow beta features to be emulated. So if the cluster starts to use the beta apis by enabling the beta feature gate, we need support them in emulated version.

that is the paradox we have with the combo feature that depends on API, take a feature like ServiceCIDR that is exactly with @Jefftree is describing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128971

The feature and the API moves at the same time, the API without the feature (controllers, ...) is useless, why do you want to emulate an API like that? In addition, the cluster does not even start if the feature is not enabled, and if you enable it it fails becuse is looking for the GA API that does not exist in the previous version

Check the failure in the test `k8s.io/kubernetes/test/integration: etcd ` in https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/128971/pull-kubernetes-integration/1873855559963250688 , the test `=== RUN   TestEtcdStoragePath/1.31` fails  to start because is not able to find the GA APIS , needed by the controllers to work

EDIT 

to be more clear, the problem is not to emulate the APIs is to emulate the feature gates that depend on the APIs

| Feature Gate | API | Binary Version | Emulated Version | Result |
|--------------|-----|---------------|------------------|----|
| GA | v1 | 1.33 |  - | ok |
| Beta | v1beta1 | 1.33 |  1.32 | controller depends on v1 and fails|

> 
> AFAIK APIs are not feature gated and they should be using a stored version n-1 , so there should not be any need for handling the APIs
> 
Does the storage version policy of n-1 need be changed to n-3 for emulation version then?

> The KEP is to make upgrades safer based on the hypothesis that being able to emulate features we are able to make this safe path, but we are emulating business logic and duplicating code paths that can drift or have copy paste errors or will need backports ... debugging and troubleshooting will be really complex and will add a lot of overhead to the feature owners ... I'm skeptical that this approach will make the upgrade safer than with today's methid since we are "faking" the emulation and we may have copy paste errors ... I don't think there is enough return on investment

I agree to a certain extent, if we are duplicating a lot of business logic and code paths, the overhead will make it difficult for maintenance. That's the exact reason we're not emulating alphas because they're more unstable and business logic could change drastically between alphas and betas describing the exact scenario you mentioned with the overhead. For beta->GA, generally the changes in business logic and API is more contained and in a lot of scenarios almost a duplicate of the types from beta -> GA. Thus, I think it's worth an effort for us to try to support beta->GA rather than dropping support for complex features that depend on API. A quick scan through https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128971 seems to suggest mostly a `s/v1beta1/v1` operation for beta->GA type which I feel like we *should* be able to safely emulate with the right changes.

> Does the storage version policy of n-1 need be changed to n-3 for emulation version then?

With compatibility versions, storage version defaults to `minCompatVersion` which is `emulatedVersion - 1` == `n-1` by default. Given the two parameters, we're technically widening the net to support `{n-3,...,n}` (n because we could set `minCompatVersion = emulationVersion` and disallow downgrades). I think we could update the documentation to indicate this range of support?
/cc @liggitt

> For beta->GA, generally the changes in business logic and API is more contained and in a lot of scenarios almost a duplicate of the types from beta -> GA. Thus, I think it's worth an effort for us to try to support beta->GA rather than dropping support for complex features that depend on API. A quick scan through #128971 seems to suggest mostly a `s/v1beta1/v1` operation for beta->GA type which I feel like we _should_ be able to safely emulate with the right changes.

ServiceCIDR is a very simple API ... if you check at DRA you'll see that is not as straightforward ... if we can not generalize that, we can not be consistent and then emulating a beta feature that is disabled by default does not provide enough benefit vs the cost of maintenance and the developer experience ...

Since 
1. it is impractical to use switch statements everywhere in the code.
2. it seems very difficult to design a generic enough interface/wrapper around the versions

We will probably need to emulate serving the new API somehow. 
If that is the case, why don't we just not removing the new APIs for emulated version in the apiserver in the first place?

We would need to reframe the purpose of emulated version for APIs: it is more about keeping the removed APIs (Beta and GA) in emulation mode. As for API versions introduced after the emulated version, it is ok to serve and use them because the underlying storage version is the same. This should be ok since most likely Beta->GA APIs do not change much. 

WDYT? @jpbetz @liggitt @aojea

review_comments: having a comment explaining what are the condition to consider a gv not removed can help future us to understand that this method should implement
not familiar with this structure, can there be any ordered problems, per example that we break too early and miss to enable versions?
this iteration is based on `PrioritizedVersionsForGroup` so they should be already ordered by priority. We do not want to enable versions that have lower priority.
